question:
During a classroom investigation on organising numerical data, three groups P, Q and R record the number of practice sheets completed on four consecutive days. Their record is represented by the matrix $A=\begin{bmatrix}12&15&18&20\\10&14&16&19\\8&12&15&17\end{bmatrix}$. The rows, in order, represent groups P, Q and R, while the columns represent Day 1, Day 2, Day 3 and Day 4. The teacher writes the matrix in general notation as $A=[a_{ij}]$, where $a_{ij}$ denotes the entry in the $i$th row and $j$th column. A second record $B=[b_{ij}]$ is prepared in the same arrangement and satisfies $b_{ij}=a_{ij}$ for every corresponding position.

(a) Determine the order of $A$ and the total number of its elements.

(b) Find $a_{23}$ and interpret its meaning in the given situation.

(c) Write the second row of $A$ separately as a matrix and identify its type and order.

(d) Determine whether $A$ and $B$ are equal matrices. Justify your conclusion using the conditions for equality of matrices.
explanation:
(a)
The matrix $A$ has 3 rows and 4 columns. Therefore, its order is $3\times4$. The number of elements in an $m\times n$ matrix is $mn$. Hence, the total number of elements is $3\times4=12$. Thus, $A$ is an ordered rectangular array having 12 entries.

(b)
In the notation $A=[a_{ij}]$, $a_{ij}$ denotes the entry in the $i$th row and $j$th column. Therefore, $a_{23}$ is the entry in the second row and third column. From $A$, $a_{23}=16$. Since the second row represents group Q and the third column represents Day 3, the value 16 means that group Q completed 16 practice sheets on Day 3.

(c)
The second row of $A$ is $\begin{bmatrix}10&14&16&19\end{bmatrix}$. It has one row and four columns, so its order is $1\times4$. A matrix having only one row is called a row matrix. Hence, the required matrix is a row matrix of order $1\times4$.

(d)
Two matrices are equal when they have the same order and all corresponding elements are equal. Both $A$ and $B$ have the same arrangement, and it is given that $b_{ij}=a_{ij}$ for every corresponding position. Therefore, all corresponding entries are equal. Hence, $A=B$.

options.A:
(a) Order $4\times3$; 12 elements.
(b) $a_{23}=16$, representing group Q on Day 3.
(c) $\begin{bmatrix}10&14&16&19\end{bmatrix}$ is a row matrix of order $1\times4$.
(d) $A=B$ because corresponding entries are equal.
options.B:
(a) Order $3\times4$; 12 elements.
(b) $a_{23}=15$, representing group Q on Day 3.
(c) $\begin{bmatrix}10&14&16&19\end{bmatrix}$ is a row matrix of order $1\times4$.
(d) $A=B$ because corresponding entries are equal.
options.C:
(a) Order $3\times4$; 12 elements.
(b) $a_{23}=16$, representing 16 practice sheets completed by group Q on Day 3.
(c) $\begin{bmatrix}10&14&16&19\end{bmatrix}$ is a row matrix of order $1\times4$.
(d) $A=B$ because they have the same order and every pair of corresponding entries is equal.
options.D:
(a) Order $3\times4$; 12 elements.
(b) $a_{23}=16$, representing group Q on Day 3.
(c) $\begin{bmatrix}10&14&16&19\end{bmatrix}$ is a column matrix of order $4\times1$.
(d) $A\ne B$ because the matrices have different names.
